**Direction: The Ripple Loom**

**The claim.** A thought is not a token sequence; it is a traveling wave that leaves a ripple wake. Quilt 2036 makes that literal. Ideas live on the quilt grid (the SuperInstance's cell lattice) as three coupled field phenomena: (1) **traveling waves** — phase fronts that sweep across cells, implementing Muller's spatiotemporal generative computation as motion over the map; (2) **ripples** — ~90Hz-local save/replay events that bind the currently-coherent distributed state into a durable granule; (3) **spirals** — phase singularities pinned at network boundaries that rotate a task's top-down/bottom-up flow and act as the "attention rotor" for the active idea. The kernel's five opcodes are the field's control surface: BIND writes a phase relationship between two cells (a wave source), LINK fixes a spiral core at a boundary, EFFECT emits a ripple (commit), VIEW samples the field at a point, TICK advances the wave equation one step. Nothing is a token; everything is a phase.

**Mechanism — ideas as field phenomena.** Each Quilt cell carries a complex amplitude and a local phase. TICK integrates a wave equation with two nonlinearities: a boundary term that nucleates spirals where phase gradients are steep (Xu/Gong's boundary condition), and a ripple gate that fires when local coherence crosses a threshold — the Verzhbinsky save event. A ripple does not store activations; it stores the *phase configuration* of the cells that co-fired, plus the spiral's winding number and rotation sense. That tuple is the granule. Consciousness, per Vishne, is then a dynamical property: a Quilt state is "conscious" of an idea when its ventral-stream-analog cells (feature maps) and prefrontal-analog cells (spiral cores) are phase-locked through a ripple train, and "unconscious" when the same content exists only as a decaying wave without a ripple commit. The JEPA-predictive GravityField proposes the next wave source; surprise is the residual between predicted phase field and measured phase field. OTOC lambda becomes the wave's Lyapunov exponent on the lattice — high lambda means the idea is chaotic and forks easily; low lambda means it is a stable attractor.

**Rewind at granule resolution.** Every ripple is a ledger entry in the FNV-chained witness log: canonical JSON of {cell phases, spiral cores, winding numbers, MOTH draw id, JEV verdict, parent granule hash}. Rewind is not checkpoint-restore; it is **re-injection**: you take any granule, re-seed the field with its phase configuration, and TICK forward. Because the wave equation is deterministic given the seed and the MOTH-certified entropy draw, replay is bit-exact and verifiable against the ledger. Forking is free — inject the same granule with a different MOTH seed and you get a sibling trajectory. Granularity is the ripple, not the token: you can rewind to the exact moment a spiral flipped rotation sense, which is the exact moment the idea changed its mind.

**JEV/MOTH/ML interlock.** MOTHQuantum supplies the certified entropy that seeds each ripple's phase jitter — this is what makes replays reproducible yet non-degenerate, and the CHSH witness is embedded in the granule so a forked run can prove it used fresh entropy. The JEV gate scores each proposed wave source before it is allowed to nucleate a spiral: canon sources (consistent with the ledger's prior phase history) pass; speculation sources are quarantined into a shadow field that can be VIEWed but not BINDed into the main lattice. ML — the JEPA predictor — sits between them: it proposes wave sources, MOTH perturbs them, JEV adjudicates, and the OTOC dial reports the ruggedness of the resulting landscape so the runtime can auto-tune lambda toward either exploration (high) or consolidation (low). The interlock is a loop: predict → perturb → judge → commit → measure ruggedness → re-tune.

**First 90 days.** Weeks 1–3: implement a 2D complex-phase lattice on the existing kernel; TICK as a leapfrog integrator; VIEW as point sampling. Weeks 4–6: ripple detector (coherence threshold + co-fire window), granule serializer, FNV ledger extension, and a replay CLI that re-injects a granule and diffs the resulting phase field. Weeks 7–9: spiral nucleation at boundaries (LINK), rotation-sense tracking, and the JEV gate wired to the granule serializer so every commit carries a verdict. Weeks 10–12: MOTH seeding of ripple jitter with CHSH witness embedded; JEPA predictor as wave-source proposer; OTOC lambda measured on the lattice and exposed as a dial. Deliverable: a runnable demo where a user plays an idea, forks it at a chosen ripple, and replays both branches to bit-exact divergence — with the ledger proving which MOTH draw and JEV verdict each branch used.

**Falsifiable prediction.** If ripples are the save/replay event, then injecting a ripple at a phase-incoherent moment (coherence below threshold) should fail to produce a stable granule — replaying it should decay within N ticks, while a ripple at coherence peak should replay stably for ≥10N ticks. Measure the survival ratio across 1000 seeded trials; the Ripple Loom predicts a sharp threshold, a feedforward transformer baseline predicts no threshold. If the threshold is absent, the direction is wrong.

The Ripple Loom

**Ripple Loom**

Quilt becomes a phase field. Every granule is a node with NOUL type, amplitude, phase, and witness hash. Ideas are not tokens passed forward; they are traveling waves, ripples, and spiral phase singularities moving over the quilt grid. `BIND` phase-locks distant granules into an assembly. `LINK` sets waveguide delays between them. `EFFECT` applies local gain, inhibition, and nonlinearity. `VIEW` samples the field. `TICK` integrates the wave equation. Sensory history and generative prediction are encoded as motion over maps: a wavefront carries its past in its phase gradient and its future in its JEPA-predicted target. Spiral waves nucleate at boundaries between modules—visual, prefrontal, motor—and their rotation direction gates bottom-up versus top-down flow per task. Ripples are the save/replay events: when local coherence crosses a threshold, the active assembly is compressed into a 90Hz ripple packet. Replaying that packet reinstates stimulus-selective firing across distant granules. Conscious content is the trajectory of these field phenomena, not a static code.

Rewind is granule-resolution because every `TICK` writes a canonical JSON witness entry: granule id, phase, amplitude, incoming `LINK` delays, `EFFECT` params, `VIEW` sample, MOTH job citation, JEV score, OTOC lambda, and FNV-chained hash. Refusals are hash-committed too. To rewind, query the ledger for a granule’s last stable ripple packet, reconstruct its local phase field, and re-run `TICK` deterministically with MOTH-certified entropy. You can rewind a single granule, a spiral arm, or an arbitrary `VIEW`-selected set. Forking creates a new ledger branch at any granule event. The ripple packet is the save state; the granule is the unit. You can rewind one idea’s phase without rewinding the whole thought.

JEV, MOTH, and ML interlock concretely. MOTH supplies certified entropy for `TICK` noise, spiral nucleation, and fork tie-breaking; each job is cited in the ledger and CHSH-witnessed, so no hidden determinism can masquerade as field dynamics. ML—specifically the JEPA-predictive proposer in GravityField—predicts the next latent field patch. Surprise is prediction error weighted by local amplitude. High surprise triggers a ripple save; low surprise permits compressed `TICK` advance. JEV gates every candidate ripple and fork: its typesafe NOUL oracle scores canon versus speculation by checking NOUL type consistency across linked granules, witness-chain validity, and OTOC effect. Canon ripples commit as stable memory. Speculation ripples go to the fork pool. Spiral rotation is also a JEV decision—bottom-up or top-down—based on task type and NOUL context. The OTOC chaos dial sets lambda: high lambda means a rugged landscape, shorter ripples, more exploratory forks; low lambda means stable replay and long ripples.

First 90-day build:

Weeks 1–2: define the ripple packet schema in canonical JSON. Extend `TICK` to compute phase field using existing opcodes only: `BIND` phase-locks, `LINK` sets delay, `EFFECT` applies gain, `VIEW` samples. No new opcodes.

Weeks 3–4: implement a 1D/2D wave simulator with a 90Hz ripple detector. Seed noise from MOTH. Record every `TICK` in the FNV ledger.

Weeks 5–6: build the granule rewind API. Query by granule id or time, reconstruct phase state, fork the ledger, and verify replay against the original witness chain.

Weeks 7–8: integrate JEPA as the GravityField proposer. Surprise-triggered ripples save the field. Compare surprise-weighted forks to random forks.

Weeks 9–10: wire JEV to score ripples and spiral rotation for canon versus speculation. Calibrate OTOC lambda against task difficulty.

Weeks 11–12: run a two-site working-memory task. Bind two stimuli, let a traveling wave cross, trigger a ripple, rewind from the ripple packet, and measure reinstatement across distant sites.

Falsifiable prediction: In that two-site task, replaying a single 90Hz ripple packet from the ledger will reinstate stimulus-selective firing across distant sites with >90% phase coherence and <5% JEV speculation leakage, while a feedforward transformer baseline will score <60% on the same reinstatement metric. If not, the field model is falsified.

Ripple Loom

# THE RIPPLE CANON

The move: stop storing ideas as granules-of-data and start storing them as events-of-field. The quilt grid becomes an excitable medium. Thinking is wave motion. Canon is what survives replay.

**(a) Mechanism.** The grid is a lattice of granules, each holding (phase, amplitude, content-hash). Four opcodes become field operators: LINK lays anisotropic waveguides — Muller's traveling waves need direction; BIND phase-locks distant clusters so they co-fire, making distributed working memory a bound oscillator instead of a shared token; EFFECT is a wavefront changing mode at a boundary; VIEW samples the field. TICK is the ripple: cortex saves at ~90Hz; here, one sharp sweep per tick traverses active granules and reads them out — the Verzhbinsky save/replay event. Ideas propagate as waves; sensory history is embedded in wavefront shape, so generation is literally motion over the map, not feedforward tokens. Where bottom-up surprise (JEPA prediction error) meets top-down canon priors, wavefronts collide and curl into spirals. Phase singularities — spiral cores — are the system's operators: chirality sets task mode (one rotation explores, the other consolidates), pinning a singularity spawns a fork boundary, annihilating opposite charges merges ideas. Per Vishne, a pattern is conscious/canon only if replaying the field reproduces its trajectory — representational recurrence. Everything else is a ghost-ripple: visible in VIEW, never authoritative. The Quilt SuperInstance is the frame itself: the inter-transformer reads the entire superstate at each ripple instead of transforming tokens locally.

**(b) Rewind at granule resolution.** Every TICK appends a field frame to the witness ledger: per-granule deltas (phase, amplitude, hash, incoming wave sources) in canonical JSON, FNV-chained; JEV refusals hash-committed alongside. Kernel plus seeded OTOC lambda plus job-cited QRNG make each tick deterministic, so rewind is exact re-injection: load frame N, seed the recorded phases, re-TICK — bit-reproducible and replay-verifiable, the ledger property extended from events to fields. Granular rewind walks one granule's chain backwards to its last phase change, extracts the causal wedge of waves that touched it, and forks from that frame. Both branches are witnessed; the OTOC dial measures echo decay between branch and trunk — the chaos dial becomes the divergence meter. Scrubbing the timeline slices thought into per-tick frames playable at any speed: the rewindable granulate substrate, literally.

**(c) The interlock.** MOTHQuantum's CHSH-witnessed entropy chooses each ripple's nucleation point — where a wave is born is unforgeable and job-cited in the ledger, so no speculation can be retro-rationalized. The JEPA predictor proposes the next wavefront from embedded history; prediction error against the actual field is surprise, which weights GravityField's lamp-pull and retunes LINK anisotropy — learning is waveguide reshaping. JEV's NOUL oracle sits at the ripple: it admits frames meeting canon invariants (types, ledger consistency, dynamical recurrence); the rest are quarantined as ghost-ripples with committed refusals. Division of labor: JEPA proposes the wave, MOTH guarantees its freedom, OTOC prices its consequences, JEV decides what becomes canon.

**(d) First 90 days.** Days 1–30: rebuild TICK as a ripple sweep on a 64×64 granule field; granule state becomes the phase/amplitude/hash tuple; append field frames to the existing ledger; prove bit-exact replay of a 10k-tick run. Days 31–60: LINK anisot
